app.name: Tre
q.states.ice.sun.prompt: You leave a piece of ice in the sun. What does it become?
q.states.ice.sun.hint: The sun makes things warm. What does warm ice do?
q.states.ice.sun.explain: Ice melts into water when it gets warm.
q.states.fire.out.prompt: What can put out a fire?
q.states.fire.out.hint: Fire does not like to get wet.
q.states.fire.out.explain: Water puts out fire. It makes the fire cool and wet.
q.states.boil.prompt: Water boils in a pot. What rises from the pot?
q.states.boil.hint: Very hot water goes up like a white cloud.
q.states.boil.explain: Hot water becomes steam. Steam is water as a gas.
q.states.freeze.prompt: You put water in a very cold place. What does it become?
q.states.freeze.explain: Water freezes into ice when it gets very cold.
q.states.back.prompt: Ice melts into water. Can that water become ice again?
q.states.back.hint: Think about a freezer. It makes water cold.
q.states.back.explain: Water can change back and forth when it gets hot and cold.
q.states.back.c1: Yes, if it gets cold again
q.states.ash.prompt: Which change can NOT go back?
q.states.ash.explain: Ash cannot become wood again. Water and ice can change back and forth.
q.mat.iron.prompt: Which thing is made of iron?
q.mat.iron.explain: The smith's hammer is iron. The hat is made of leaves. The basket is made of bamboo.
q.mat.hard.hint: Which one can you not bend with your hands?
q.mat.hard.explain: Iron is harder than straw and cloth.
q.mat.heat.prompt: The smith heats iron in the fire. What happens to the iron?
q.mat.heat.hint: Fire makes the iron very hot.
q.mat.heat.explain: Fire makes iron hot. Hot iron is softer, so the smith can shape it.
q.mat.heat.c1: It gets hot and soft, so it bends
q.mat.float.hint: Bamboo is hollow. It has air inside.
q.mat.float.explain: Bamboo is light and has air inside, so it floats. The nail and the stone sink.
q.mat.pot.prompt: Why is a rice pot made of metal, not paper?
q.mat.pot.hint: What happens to paper in a fire?
q.mat.pot.explain: Paper burns in a fire. Metal does not burn, and it carries the heat to the rice.
q.mat.pot.c1: Metal does not burn, and it carries heat well
q.water.down.hint: Pour water on a tilted board. Where does it go?
q.water.down.explain: Water always flows down, from high places to low places.
q.water.down.c1: From high places to low places
q.water.down.c2: Up to the top of the hill
q.water.rain.prompt: Where does rain water go after the rain?
q.water.rain.hint: Look at the yard after the rain.
q.water.rain.explain: Rain water flows into rivers and ponds, and it goes into the ground.
q.water.rain.c1: Into rivers, ponds, and the ground
q.water.sea.hint: The sea is in the lowest place.
q.water.sea.explain: Rivers flow from the mountains to the plains, and then to the sea.
q.water.canal.prompt: Why do farmers dig small canals to their rice fields?
q.water.canal.hint: What does rice need to grow?
q.water.canal.explain: Rice needs a lot of water. A canal brings water from the river to the field.
q.water.canal.c1: To bring water to the rice
q.float.boat.prompt: An iron nail sinks, but a big iron boat floats. Why?
q.float.boat.hint: The boat is hollow in the middle.
q.float.boat.explain: The boat is wide and hollow. It pushes a lot of water away, so the water holds it up.
q.float.boat.c1: The boat's shape holds a lot of air and pushes away a lot of water
q.float.boat.c3: The boat is lighter than the nail
q.float.sink.hint: Which one is heavy and solid?
q.float.sink.explain: A stone is solid and heavy for its size, so it sinks.
q.float.raft.prompt: A raft carries too many bags of rice. What can happen?
q.float.raft.hint: What does a heavier load do to the raft?
q.float.raft.explain: More weight pushes the raft lower. Too much weight makes it sink.
q.float.raft.c1: It goes lower and can sink
q.earth.ocean.prompt: Where is most of the water on Earth?
q.earth.ocean.hint: Look at a globe. The blue part is water.
q.earth.ocean.explain: The oceans hold most of the water on Earth. Ocean water is salty.
q.earth.tide.prompt: The sea goes up and down each day (the tide). What pulls the water?
q.earth.tide.hint: A big round thing in the night sky.
q.earth.tide.explain: The Moon pulls the sea water, so the tide goes up and down.
q.earth.fresh.prompt: Where is most of the fresh water on Earth?
q.earth.fresh.hint: Fresh water is not salty. Most of it is frozen.
q.earth.fresh.explain: Most fresh water is ice, at the poles and on high mountains.
q.needs.plant.prompt: What does a plant need to grow?
q.needs.plant.hint: Grandma waters the plants each day and puts them in the sun.
q.needs.plant.explain: Plants need water, light, air, and good soil to grow.
q.needs.buffalo.prompt: What does a water buffalo need to live?
q.needs.buffalo.hint: What do you need each day?
q.needs.buffalo.explain: Animals need food, water, and air to live.
q.needs.dark.prompt: A rice plant stays in a dark box for many days. What happens?
q.needs.dark.hint: A plant needs light to make its food.
q.needs.dark.explain: With no light, the plant cannot make food. It gets weak and yellow.
q.needs.dark.c3: It turns into a big tree
q.needs.bee.prompt: Bees go from flower to flower. How do they help the plants?
q.needs.bee.hint: Yellow dust sticks to the legs of the bee.
q.needs.bee.explain: Bees carry pollen. Then the flowers can make fruit and seeds.
q.needs.bee.c1: They carry pollen from flower to flower
q.animals.chicken.prompt: How many legs does a chicken have?
q.animals.fish.hint: Watch a fish move in the water.
q.animals.fish.explain: A fish uses its fins and tail to swim.
q.animals.spider.prompt: How many legs does a spider have?
q.animals.spider.hint: A spider has more legs than an ant. An ant has 6 legs.
q.animals.turtle.prompt: Why does a turtle have a hard shell?
q.animals.turtle.hint: When a turtle is afraid, where does its head go?
q.animals.turtle.explain: The hard shell keeps the turtle safe.
q.animals.duck.prompt: Baby ducks follow their mother. Why?
q.animals.duck.hint: What do parents do for their young?
q.animals.duck.explain: Animal parents keep their young safe and teach them to find food.
q.animals.duck.c1: She keeps them safe and shows them food
q.habitat.lotus.prompt: Where does a lotus plant live?
q.habitat.lotus.explain: The lotus lives in ponds. Its roots are in the mud.
q.habitat.lotus.c1: In ponds with mud and water
q.habitat.frog.prompt: Which animal lives in the water of a rice field?
q.habitat.frog.hint: This animal jumps well and says "ribbit".
q.habitat.frog.explain: Frogs live in wet places, like rice fields.
q.habitat.birds.prompt: Why do many birds fly south when it gets cold?
q.habitat.birds.hint: In the cold season there are few insects to eat.
q.habitat.birds.explain: The birds go to warmer places with more food.
q.habitat.birds.c1: To find warm places and food
q.body.heart.hint: Put your hand on your chest. What do you feel?
q.body.heart.explain: The heart beats to move blood around the body.
q.body.heart.c1: It moves blood around the body
q.body.roots.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
q.body.roots.hint: This part is under the ground.
q.body.roots.explain: Roots take in water and food from the soil.
q.body.lungs.hint: Breathe in deeply. Your chest gets bigger.
q.body.lungs.explain: The lungs take in air when you breathe in.
q.body.lungs.c1: They take air into the body
q.chain.sun.prompt: A buffalo eats grass. In this food chain, where does the energy come from first?
q.chain.sun.hint: What does grass need to make its food?
q.chain.sun.explain: Grass uses sunlight to make food. The buffalo eats the grass.
q.chain.producer.prompt: Which living thing makes its own food?
q.chain.producer.hint: It needs light, water, and air.
q.chain.producer.explain: Green plants make food from light. Animals must eat plants or other animals.
q.chain.decompose.prompt: Leaves fall and rot on the ground. What helps break them down?
q.chain.decompose.explain: Worms and fungi break down leaves and make the soil better for plants.
q.weather.clouds.prompt: Dark clouds fill the sky. What may come soon?
q.weather.clouds.hint: Dark clouds hold a lot of water.
q.weather.cold.prompt: What should you wear on a cold day?
q.weather.cold.explain: A warm coat keeps your body warm.
q.weather.rainbow.prompt: When can we see a rainbow?
q.weather.rainbow.hint: A rainbow needs sunlight and water drops.
q.weather.rainbow.explain: Sunlight goes through rain drops and splits into many colors.
q.weather.rainbow.c1: When the sun shines while it rains
q.weather.season.prompt: In the north of Vietnam, which season is the coldest?
q.weather.season.hint: The Tết new year comes near its end.
q.weather.season.explain: The north has four seasons. Winter is the coldest.
q.land.mountain.prompt: Which is higher: a mountain or a hill?
q.land.mountain.hint: A hill is low and round.
q.land.mountain.explain: A mountain is higher than a hill.
q.land.map.prompt: On a map, which color often shows water?
q.land.map.hint: Think about the color of the sea.
q.land.map.explain: Maps often show rivers, lakes, and seas in blue.
q.land.slow.prompt: Rain falls on a hill for many years. What can happen to the hill?
q.land.slow.hint: Moving water carries soil and sand.
q.land.slow.explain: Rain water carries soil away very slowly, over many years.
q.land.slow.c1: The rain slowly washes soil away
q.climate.diff.prompt: What is the difference between weather and climate?
q.climate.diff.hint: One of them changes each day.
q.climate.diff.explain: Weather changes each day. Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
q.climate.diff.c1: Weather is today; climate is the usual weather over many years
q.climate.stilts.prompt: Why do people build houses on stilts in places with floods?
q.climate.stilts.hint: In a flood, the water goes up.
q.climate.stilts.explain: A house on stilts is above the ground, so flood water stays out.
q.climate.stilts.c1: To stay dry when the water rises
q.climate.hot.prompt: Which place is usually hot all year?
q.climate.hot.hint: The equator is the line around the middle of the Earth.
q.climate.hot.explain: Places near the equator get the most sunlight, so they are hot all year.
q.climate.hot.c2: A place near the North Pole
q.climate.hot.c3: The top of a snowy mountain
q.erosion.valley.prompt: What makes a river valley deeper over a long time?
q.erosion.valley.hint: Water that flows for a long time wears down stone.
q.erosion.valley.explain: River water flows for many years. It wears the rock and makes the valley deeper.
q.erosion.valley.c1: Moving water wears the rock away
q.erosion.trees.prompt: Why do people plant trees on hills?
q.erosion.trees.hint: Roots are like ropes in the soil.
q.erosion.trees.explain: Roots hold the soil, so the rain does not wash it away.
q.erosion.layers.prompt: In layers of rock, which layer is usually the oldest?
q.erosion.layers.hint: Which layer was put down first?
q.erosion.layers.explain: New layers cover old layers, so the bottom layer is usually the oldest.
q.space.day.prompt: Why do we have day and night?
q.space.day.hint: Spin a ball in front of a lamp.
q.space.day.explain: The Earth spins. The side that faces the Sun has day. The other side has night.
q.space.day.c2: Because the Sun turns off at night
q.space.shadow.prompt: When is your shadow the shortest?
q.space.shadow.hint: When is the Sun highest in the sky?
q.space.shadow.explain: At noon the Sun is highest, so shadows are shortest.
q.space.sun.prompt: Why does the Sun look bigger than other stars?
q.space.sun.hint: Things that are close look bigger than things far away.
q.space.sun.explain: The Sun is a star. It is much closer to us than the other stars.
q.space.sun.c1: It is much closer to us
q.space.sun.c2: It is the biggest star of all
q.forces.cart.prompt: How can you make a heavy cart move?
q.forces.cart.hint: A force is a push or a pull.
q.forces.cart.explain: To move a thing, you must push or pull it.
q.forces.cart.c2: Look at it for a long time
q.forces.friction.prompt: A ball rolls on grass and stops. What stops it?
q.forces.friction.hint: The rough grass rubs against the ball.
q.forces.friction.explain: Friction is a force between two surfaces that rub. It slows the ball.
q.forces.balanced.prompt: Two children pull a rope with the same force in opposite directions. What does the rope do?
q.forces.balanced.hint: When two forces are equal, which side wins?
q.forces.balanced.explain: Equal forces in opposite directions are balanced. The rope stays still.
q.energy.spoon.prompt: A metal spoon stays in hot soup. After some time, what is the handle like?
q.energy.spoon.explain: Heat moves from the soup through the metal spoon to the handle.
q.energy.drum.prompt: When you hit a drum, what does the drum skin do to make sound?
q.energy.drum.hint: Put your hand on the drum when you hit it.
q.energy.drum.explain: The drum skin vibrates. Sound is a vibration that moves through the air.
q.energy.fire.prompt: Which one gives both light and heat?
q.energy.fire.hint: What do you feel and see near a cooking fire?
q.particles.sugar.prompt: Sugar dissolves in water. Is the sugar still there?
q.particles.sugar.hint: Taste the water. Is it sweet?
q.particles.sugar.explain: The sugar is still there in tiny parts, so the water is sweet.
q.particles.sugar.c1: Yes, in tiny parts we cannot see
q.particles.balloon.prompt: Why does a balloon get bigger when you blow into it?
q.particles.balloon.explain: Air is made of tiny particles. It takes up space in the balloon.
q.particles.balloon.c1: Air is matter and takes up space
q.particles.sand.prompt: Mix sand with water, then wait. What happens?
q.particles.sand.explain: Sand does not dissolve. It is heavy, so it goes to the bottom.
q.particles.sand.c1: The sand sinks to the bottom
q.legend.bamboo.prompt: When the iron staff broke, what did Thánh Gióng use?
q.legend.bamboo.hint: This plant grows around every Vietnamese village.
q.legend.bamboo.explain: In the legend, Gióng pulled up bamboo by the road.
q.legend.smiths.prompt: Who made the iron horse for Gióng?
q.legend.smiths.hint: They work with fire and an anvil.
q.legend.smiths.explain: The smiths heated iron and made the horse, the armor, and the staff.
q.legend.village.prompt: What was the name of Gióng's village?
q.legend.village.hint: You are in this village now.
q.legend.village.explain: Gióng lived in the village of Phù Đổng. Today it is part of Hà Nội.
q.legend.storm.prompt: What does bamboo do in a storm?
q.legend.storm.hint: The name of this game means bamboo.
q.legend.storm.explain: Bamboo bends in a storm. Then it stands up again.
q.legend.storm.c1: It bends and does not break
q.legend.rice.prompt: The whole village cooked rice for Gióng. Why?
q.legend.rice.explain: In the legend, all the people shared their rice, so Gióng grew up fast to protect the land.
q.legend.rice.c1: So he could grow strong and protect the village
prob.share.each: Share {n} fruits equally among {k} friends. How many does each friend get?
prob.share.left: Share {n} fruits equally among {k} friends. How many are left over?
prob.frac.add.say: {a} over {d} plus {b} over {d} is how many over {d}?
prob.frac.unlike.say: {a} over {d1} plus {b} over {d2} is how many over {D}?
prob.area: A rectangle is {w} long and {h} wide. How many squares is its area?
prob.perimeter: A rectangle is {w} long and {h} wide. What is its perimeter?
prob.shape.name: Which one is a {shape}?
prob.shape.sides: How many sides does this shape have?
hint.count.plus10: 10 more makes the tens digit go up by 1.
hint.compare: Look at the tens first. More tens means a bigger number.
ex.compare: Example: {big} is bigger than {small}, because {bt} tens is more than {st} tens.
hint.add: Start at {a}. Then count on {b} more.
hint.add.missing: Count up from {a} to {s}. How many numbers did you count?
ex.add.missing: Example: {x} + ? = {z}. Count from {x}: {seq}. That is {y} more, so ? = {y}.
hint.addsub.add: Break the second number into parts. Add one part at a time.
hint.addsub.sub: Break the second number into parts. Take away one part at a time.
hint.place: The ones are on the right. The tens are next to them, then the hundreds.
hint.place.expanded: Write the hundreds, tens, and ones digits next to each other.
hint.share: Give one fruit to each friend, then one more round, until there are not enough for all {k} friends.
ex.share.each: Example: {p} fruits shared equally among {y} friends: {x} for each friend, and {r} left over.
ex.share.left: Example: {p} fruits shared equally among {y} friends: {x} for each friend, and {r} left over.
hint.frac.unit: When you cut a cake into more parts, each part is smaller.
hint.frac.samenum: The two fractions have the same top number. A smaller bottom number means bigger parts.
ex.frac.unit: Example: 1/{x} is bigger than 1/{y}, because {x} parts are bigger than {y} parts.
hint.frac.equiv: What times {b} makes {c}? Multiply the top number by the same number.
hint.frac.add: Keep the bottom number. Add only the top numbers.
hint.frac.unlike: First change the two fractions to the bottom number {D}. Then add the top numbers.
hint.area: Area = length × width. You can also count the squares.
hint.mul.multi: Break the first number into parts by place. Multiply each part, then add.
hint.decimal: Line up the decimal points. Then add or take away as with whole numbers.
hint.shape.sides: Touch each side and count. Count each side one time.
hint.shape.circle: A circle has no corners, like a round tray.
hint.shape.square: A square has 4 sides of the same length.
hint.shape.rectangle: A rectangle has 4 sides: 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
hint.shape.hexagon: A hexagon has 6 sides, like a cell in a beehive.
ex.shape.name: Count the sides of each shape to find the {shape}.
hint.cards.add: Pick cards that add up to {target}. Pick one card first. How much more do you need?
hint.cards.sub: Start with a big card. Take away a small card. Is the result {target}?
hint.cards.mul: Find two cards that multiply to make {target}.
ex.cards: Example: to make {target} from the cards {cards}, do {expr} = {target}.
skill.math.frac.add: Add fractions with the same bottom number
skill.math.frac.unlike: Add fractions with different bottom numbers
skill.sci.life.body: Parts of the body and of plants
world.locked: This land opens later in the story.
world.way: The way there: {km} km on roads and rivers, about {days} days.
world.arrive: You arrive after {hours} hours on the road.
road.merchant: A merchant on the road shares a bowl of rice with you.
road.rain: Rain falls. You wait under a big tree until it stops.
road.cart: You help a farmer push a cart out of the mud. The farmer gives you a coin.
road.ferry: A ferry takes you over a wide river.
road.song: Children sing a song by the road. The way feels short.
map.ore.found: You found iron ore! The iron goes into your bag.
map.ore.look: A rock with dark, shiny spots. Maybe it is iron ore.
map.road.early: This road goes to Thăng Long, to [[vanmieu]]. Help the villagers first.
map.sign.vanmieu: The sign shows the way to [[vanmieu]], where students take exams.
map.well: The village well. The water is cool and clear.
map.banyan: The old banyan tree of the village. It is very, very old.
map.field: Green rice fields. Walk on the paths between them.
map.river: The Đuống River flows east. The water is deep here. The bridge is broken. Cross at the ford, where stones show in the low water.
gloss.vanmieu.name: Văn Miếu
gloss.phudong.name: Phù Đổng
gloss.giong.name: Thánh Gióng
gloss.giong.meaning: Saint Gióng, a hero of legend
gloss.hungvuong.name: Hùng Vương
gloss.hungvuong.meaning: a Hùng King, one of the first kings of Vietnam in legend
gloss.thanglong.name: Thăng Long
gloss.thanglong.meaning: the old name of Hà Nội
gloss.dinh.name: village hall
gloss.dinh.meaning: the big house on stilts where the village meets
gloss.tutai.name: Tú tài
gloss.song.name: Sóng
gloss.tre.name: tre
gloss.vanvo.name: văn võ song toàn
gloss.vanvo.meaning: complete in both learning and strength
gloss.nghe.name: nghề
gloss.nghe.meaning: a calling, the work of your life
gloss.an.name: the Ân army
gloss.an.meaning: the army of the Ân kingdom in the legend
gloss.thuongluong.name: thuồng luồng
gloss.thuongluong.meaning: a river serpent of Vietnamese folk tales
dlg.grandma.intro.n1: Long ago, in the time of the sixth [[hungvuong]], you are a child in the village of [[phudong]]. Your name is {name}.
dlg.grandma.intro.n2: You are an ordinary child, like all the children of the village. But every hero starts small.
dlg.grandma.intro.n3: {name}, you are awake! Today the village elder wants to see you at the [[dinh]].
dlg.grandma.intro.n4: Walk with the stick or the arrow keys, or touch and hold where you want to go. The yellow star shows where to go.
dlg.grandma.intro.nghe2.c1: Good morning, little calf! Let me give you a name.
dlg.grandma.intro.nghe1: And look who waits for you at the door: our little buffalo calf. She goes where you go.
dlg.elder.intro.n1: Hello, {name}. Our village has five skilled people: the teacher, the smith, the fisher, the healer, and the woodcutter.
dlg.elder.intro.n2: Each of them needs help with a task. These are the Five Trials. Please help all five.
dlg.elder.intro.n3: Nobody is born a hero. Like a bamboo shoot, you grow a little each day.
dlg.elder.trials.wait.n1: You have helped some of the five people. Find the others. The yellow star shows the way.
dlg.elder.trials.done.n1: You helped all five people! You have a bright mind and a kind heart.
dlg.elder.trials.done.placement: You learn fast. Go to [[vanmieu]] in Thăng Long, to the south-west. Cross the Đuống at the ford, then take the ferry over the Red River. At [[vanmieu]] there is a placement exam. It shows how far you are in your learning.
dlg.elder.trials.done.drum: Boom! Boom! Boom! A drum sounds at the [[dinh]].
dlg.elder.trials.done.n5: Listen! Someone comes from the capital. Go to the [[dinh]] and see.
dlg.elder.placement.wait.n1: Go to [[vanmieu]] for the placement exam. Go south-west: cross the Đuống at the ford, then take the ferry over the Red River.
dlg.elder.drum.n1: The drum is at the [[dinh]]. Go and see who has come.
dlg.elder.go.exam.n1: Our village is safe now. Go to [[vanmieu]] for the exam. Go south-west: cross the Đuống at the ford, then take the ferry over the Red River.
dlg.elder.idle.n1: You have grown a little more. Practice with the teacher, and keep the village safe.
dlg.elder.busy.n1: Gióng needs your help. Follow the yellow star.
dlg.teacher.wait.n1: Hello. First go and see the village elder at the [[dinh]].
dlg.teacher.trial.n1: Ah, a new student! The children need counting rods. Tie the rods of the heap into bundles of {bundle}. Put rods on the mat, and tap the straw rope to tie them.
dlg.smith.wait.n1: Hello. I am lighting the fire. Go and see the village elder first.
dlg.smith.trial.n1: You came at the right time! Bring {ore} pieces of ore to the forge, and a bucket of water from the well to the trough. Then watch the iron, and drop it into the water while it glows.
dlg.fisher.wait.n1: Hello. I am fixing my net. Go and see the village elder first.
dlg.fisher.trial.n1: Help me make a fish trap before the tide comes in. I put the first two stakes. Go on with the row to the red float, with no space wider than mine.
dlg.healer.wait.n1: Hello. I am picking healing leaves. Go and see the village elder first.
dlg.healer.trial.n1: I need three kinds of healing leaves: mugwort, perilla, and pennywort, {each} bunches of each kind. Put them in my basket, and then bring me the basket.
dlg.woodcutter.wait.n1: Hello. I am going into the forest soon. Go and see the village elder first.
dlg.woodcutter.trial.n1: This bamboo fell in the wind. Mark it with chalk for {parts} equal sticks, and then tell me to cut. Carry the sticks to the wood pile by the bridge.
dlg.teacher.practice.n1: Come and practice with me. Here, a mistake does not cost a heart. I will help you.
dlg.smith.need.iron.n1: The iron horse needs six pieces of iron. Look for iron ore in the bamboo, by the river, and near the Ân scouts outside the village gate.
dlg.smith.forge.n1: You have enough iron! Put your iron on the heap by the forge. I add some old iron too.
dlg.smith.forge.n2: The forge needs exactly {lumps} lumps. Carry the lumps into the forge, one at a time, then tap the bellows. When the iron glows, tap it to put it in the water.
dlg.smith.horse.n1: The iron horse is ready! The smith also makes the iron armor and the iron staff for Gióng. Take the good news to Gióng's house.
dlg.smith.idle.n1: The fire of my forge is always red. Come back any time.
dlg.fisher.idle.n1: The river is clear today. Remember: water flows from high places to low places.
dlg.fisher.river.n1: Some little [[thuongluong]] make trouble on our bank, west of the ford. They hide in shells of ice and bubbles of water. Remember: fire melts ice.
dlg.healer.idle.n1: Plants need water and light. People need good food and enough sleep. Remember to rest.
dlg.woodcutter.idle.n1: Bamboo bends in a storm, but it does not break. Be like the bamboo.
dlg.woodcutter.ore.n1: You are looking for iron. Right next to me, in the bamboo, there is some iron ore.
dlg.woodcutter.staffs.n1: The general comes soon. The men of the village need bamboo staffs to hold the road.
dlg.woodcutter.staffs.n2: The bamboo clump by the big road in front of the đình has a ring at each half block. Cut {staffs} staffs of the same length: slash each culm at the height of your hand, one culm at a time. The piece is as long as the height of the cut. Each slash cuts at once, so look at the rings before you slash.
dlg.woodcutter.staffs.done.n1: Good staffs, all of the same length! The men take them to Trâu Sơn with Gióng.
dlg.grandma.home.n1: You are home! Come in and rest a little.
dlg.mother.worry.n1: My little Gióng is three years old. He does not speak or laugh yet. I worry about him.
dlg.mother.idle.n1: Thank you for helping Gióng and the whole village.
dlg.giong.silent.n1: Little Gióng lies still and looks at you with big round eyes. He has not said a word yet.
dlg.giong.wait.n1: Keep looking for the iron. I know you can do it!
dlg.messenger.call.n1: A messenger of the king stands in front of the [[dinh]]. The villagers come to listen.
dlg.messenger.call.n2: People of the village! [[an]] is coming to our land. The king is looking for able people to help the country!
dlg.messenger.call.n3: We are ordinary people. We farm, we work iron, and we fish. The village needs help.
dlg.messenger.call.n4: Everyone! My little Gióng just spoke for the first time! {name}, please come to our house now!
dlg.giong.speaks.n1: Gióng was three years old. He could not speak or laugh. But today, when he heard the messenger, he spoke.
dlg.giong.speaks.n2: Mother, please ask the messenger to come in. I will go and help the country and protect our village.
dlg.giong.speaks.n3: Ask the king to make me an iron horse, an iron armor, and an iron staff.
dlg.giong.speaks.n4: My son can speak! But an iron horse is hard to make.
dlg.giong.speaks.n5: {name}, please help the smiths. I will tell you about iron and fire.
dlg.giong.speaks.n6: Iron is very hard. But in a very hot fire, iron gets soft, and the smith can shape it.
dlg.giong.speaks.n7: Then the smith puts the hot iron into water. Hiss! Steam goes up, and the iron gets hard again.
dlg.giong.speaks.n8: Remember: fire melts ice, water puts out fire, and fire and water make steam. Fire magic and water magic will help you.
dlg.giong.speaks.n9: The smith needs six pieces of iron. There is iron ore in the bamboo and by the river. Now try these two questions!
dlg.giong.rice.n1: From that day, Gióng grew very fast. He was always hungry, and new clothes were soon too small.
dlg.giong.rice.n2: We do not have enough rice. The whole village gives rice for Gióng. Please carry the trays of bowls from the path of the paddies to the pot in front of our house. For each ten bowls, Gióng grows one head taller.
dlg.giong.grown.n1: Gióng stretched, and suddenly he was a tall young man. He put on the iron armor, took the iron staff, and jumped onto the iron horse.
dlg.giong.grown.n2: Thank you, {name}, and thank you, everyone! Now I go to protect the village. Come with me!
dlg.giong.grown.n2.c1: Yes! I will come with you.
dlg.giong.grown.n3: Two soldiers of [[an]] are in the fields to the east, outside the village gate. Let us push them back together.
dlg.giong.ready.n1: Two soldiers of [[an]] are in the fields to the east. Tap them to start. I am with you!
dlg.giong.boss.n1: The general of [[an]] is at the foot of Trâu Sơn mountain, to the east. Let us go there together!
dlg.scouts.won.n1: The two Ân scouts ran back to tell their army. They left two pieces of iron.
dlg.staff.breaks.n1: Crack! The iron staff breaks in two!
dlg.bamboo.found.n1: Gióng pulls up the bamboo by the road. The bamboo bends, but it does not break!
dlg.giong.farewell.n2: Thank you, {name}. You helped me with your mind and your strength.
quest.farewell.go: Go north to the hills of Sóc Sơn.
quest.farewell.title: Gióng goes north
dlg.socson.elder.legend.n3: Yesterday some soldiers of [[an]] walked past here, on the way home to the north. One of them asked me for water. He told me that he missed his children.
dlg.socson.elder.legend.n2: Look at the bamboo by the path. It was green, and now it is yellow. People here say that the fire of the iron horse did it. They call it tre đằng ngà.
dlg.socson.elder.legend.n1: I saw a young man on an iron horse ride up the hill. I did not see him come down. My grandchildren say that he rose into the sky.
dlg.socson.elder.wait.n1: This hill is quiet. From up here, you can see the Đuống far to the south.
dlg.giong.farewell.care: Take good care of the village, and of [[nghecalf]].
dlg.giong.north.n1: The soldiers of [[an]] are gone, {name}. I ride north, to the hills of Sóc Sơn. Come and see me there.
map.ferry.back: The ferryman takes you back across the Red River.
map.ferry: The ferryman takes you and [[nghecalf]] across the Red River in his boat.
map.ferry.river: The ferryman takes you and [[nghecalf]] across the river in his boat.
map.redriver: The Red River is wide, and its water is red-brown with mud. Here only a boat can cross it.
npc.socson-elder.name: Old man of Sóc Sơn
dlg.giong.farewell.n3: Gióng turns the iron horse and rides up to the top of the hill. The clouds come down, and you do not see him any more.
dlg.patrol.intro.n1: An Ân scout came back to look around. Help keep the village safe!

gift.thanks.elder: Thank you. This will mend the roof of the village hall.
gift.thanks.smith: Thank you! I will buy more charcoal for the forge.
gift.thanks.mother: Thank you. I will cook more rice for Gióng.

raid.scouts.intro: Ân scouts walk on the road to the gate. They carry torches. Stand at the gate with your slingshot.
raid.patrol.intro: Ân scouts come back on the road to the gate.
raid.river.intro: Two little [[thuongluong]] swim up the river to the ford. They are hungry. Throw rice balls to them.
raid.soldier.intro: Ân soldiers come from the field. Hold the crossroads.
raid.boss.intro: The Ân general comes from his camp at the foot of Trâu Sơn. Gióng rides the iron horse to your side.
raid.lost: The enemies took what they could carry and left. They can come again.
raid.boss.pause: The Ân general is at the crossroads.
raid.soldier.pause: The soldiers are at the crossroads.
raid.river.pause: The little river serpents are at the ford.
raid.scouts.pause: The scouts are at the gate.
raid.tool.sling: Pull the slingshot back. Each notch of the band is one step on the road, the same as the bands on the posts.
raid.tool.gate: When a scout lifts a torch, tap the gate. The bar comes down.
raid.tool.traps: The bamboo traps are in a pile by the gate. Carry one to the road.
raid.tool.helpers: Tap a straw flag, and a villager comes to stand there.
raid.tool.nghe: Tap Nghé, and she charges at the first soldier. Only once.
raid.tool.water: Here is a jar of water. Drag the water to where you want it.
raid.tool.fire: Drag fire from the brazier. The soldiers of Ân raise wet shields when fire comes.
raid.tool.lightning: I brought my forge to the crossroads. Drag its lightning into wet ground.
raid.trap.ask: Put a trap at the {post} post.
history.giong.festival: In 2010, UNESCO listed the Gióng festival as intangible cultural heritage of humanity.
raid.river.note: The thuồng luồng is a river creature in Vietnamese folk tales.
raid.scouts.note: In the time of the sixth Hùng King, the Ân army came to the land of Văn Lang. Scouts went first to look at the roads.
raid.soldier.note: The Ân soldiers followed the orders of their king and generals. Many soldiers also missed their homes.
raid.boss.note: The battle was at the foot of Trâu Sơn mountain. Today, the Gióng festival at Phù Đổng and Sóc Sơn remembers Thánh Gióng.

home.hello: You are home! Here you choose your friends for battles, look at your titles, and rest.
home.friends: Creature friends (up to {max} in each battle)
home.no.friends: You have no creature friends yet. A calm creature can become your friend.
home.calling.none: You choose your [[nghe]] after your first exam at [[vanmieu]].

exam.passed: Congratulations, {name}! You passed and get the title {title}.
exam.stele: Your name is carved on the stone stele on the back of the turtle at [[vanmieu]].
exam.vanvo: You are strong in learning and in battle: [[vanvo]]! The bamboo grows one section.
exam.not.yet: You did not pass this time, but you keep your level. Practice these skills: {skills}. Then come back and try again!
exam.placement.done: You got {correct} of {total} right. Your math level is about {grade}. From now on, the problems match your level.
exam.who: Now you know who you are. Choose your [[nghe]].
calling.title: Choose your [[nghe]]
calling.note: A calling gives you a bonus in one subject. You can still learn all subjects. You can change your calling at home at any time.
calling.change.note: You can change your calling at any time. You lose nothing.
calling.chosen: From now on, you are a {calling}.
vanmieu.hello: Hello. This is [[vanmieu]]. Students come here to take exams. Are you ready?
vanmieu.hello.placement: Hello. You are in a higher grade. Take the placement exam, so that the game matches your level.
vanmieu.hello.done: Hello, {name}! Your name is on the stele. Keep learning and practicing.
vanmieu.note: Văn Miếu in Thăng Long was built in 1070. In 1076, Quốc Tử Giám, the first university of Vietnam, opened here. From 1484, the names of the doctors were carved on stone steles on the backs of stone turtles. In the game, you travel to Văn Miếu for exams, but the story of Thánh Gióng is from much earlier.
time.warn: {n} minutes are left before rest time.
time.rest: It is time to rest, {name}. Grandma saved your game. See you tomorrow!

dlg.river.friends.n1: The two little [[thuongluong]] are calm now. [[nghecalf]] comes close and sniffs them. She is not afraid.
dlg.river.friends.n4: The smallest [[thuongluong]] stays and looks at you.
dlg.river.friends.n5: Thank you for melting my cold shell of ice. I want to come with you too!
dlg.river.friends.n5.c1: Welcome! Let me give you a name.
dlg.river.friends.n6: [[song]] is also your friend. In battles, [[song]] makes a shield of water. Your first mistake does not cost a heart.
dlg.river.friends.n7: [[song]] waves its tail and swims back to the river.

dlg.teacher.trial.done.n1: Thank you! Now I can count the rods fast, a bundle at a time. A person who loves numbers and books is a Scholar.
dlg.smith.trial.done.n1: Listen to that hiss! Hot iron that meets cold water becomes hard. A person who works with iron and fire is a Smith.
dlg.fisher.trial.done.n1: Look, the fish stayed in the trap! A person who lives with the river is a Fisher.
dlg.healer.trial.done.n1: Just right, {each} bunches of each kind. Now I can make medicine. A person who takes care of plants and people is a Healer.
dlg.woodcutter.trial.done.n1: Good, equal sticks for the bridge. A person of the forest is a Woodcutter.
event.cart.start: The wheel of my cart is stuck in the mud. The hole takes {need} stones. Bring stones to the hole, then call me to push.
event.cart.short: The cart still sinks. The hole needs more stones.
event.cart.over: Too many: some stones roll out.
event.cart.done: The cart is out! Thank you.
event.flood.start: The heavy rain flooded my field. {need} pails of water must go into the ditch. Carry the water to the ditch, then call me.
event.flood.short: The field is still too wet. More water must go.
event.flood.over: Too much: the field gets dry. Some water goes back.
event.flood.done: Just right for the rice. Thank you!
event.market.start: It is market day. A rice ball costs {need} coins. Put the coins on the mat, then call me.
event.market.over: That is too much. Take some back.
event.market.done: Just right! Here is your rice.
event.market.poor: You do not have enough coins. Come back another day.
event.duck.start: My flock has {need} ducks, all white with green heads, and some are lost. The brown ducks are from another farm. Find my ducks, bring them to the pen, and call me to count.
event.duck.short: I count, and the flock is not all here. Some are still lost.
event.duck.over: A brown duck is from another farm. I let it go home.
event.duck.done: The whole flock is home! Thank you.
edge.mist: The south is still in the mist.
edge.mist.far: The land ahead is still in the mist.
dlg.teacher.practice.end.n1: Well done, {name}! All the rods are in bundles. Thank you. Now you choose: stay and play on, or go back.
dlg.smith.practice.end.n1: The iron is hard. Good work, {name}! Thank you. Now you choose: stay and play on, or go back.
dlg.fisher.practice.end.n1: All the fish stayed in the trap, {name}! Thank you. Now you choose: stay and play on, or go back.
dlg.healer.practice.end.n1: Now I have all the herbs, {name}. Thank you very much. Now you choose: stay and play on, or go back.
dlg.woodcutter.practice.end.n1: All the sticks are equal, {name}! Thank you. Now you choose: stay and play on, or go back.
practiceLink.bo-que.title: Bundles of ten
practiceLink.bo-que.line: Tie the counting rods into bundles of ten for the teacher: counting, and tens.
practiceLink.ren-sat.title: At the forge
practiceLink.ren-sat.line: Bring ore and water to the forge, and drop the hot iron into the water at the right time: hot, cold, and materials.
practiceLink.cam-coc.title: The fish trap
practiceLink.cam-coc.line: Put stakes in a row in the river, with no space wider than the first space: lengths, and sums.
practiceLink.hai-thuoc.title: Herbs for the healer
practiceLink.hai-thuoc.line: Put the same number of each herb in the basket of the healer: counting, and equal groups.
practiceLink.chat-tre.title: Equal sticks
practiceLink.chat-tre.line: Mark a bamboo stem and cut it into equal sticks for the woodcutter: lengths, and equal parts.
practiceLink.unknown: This practice link is not known. Choose an adventure.
practiceLink.pick: Practice: {title}. Who plays? Choose your profile.
parent.links.about: Send a link to your child: the child plays one activity at once, with the profile of the child, and the progress is saved. The link has only the name of the activity, and no data of the child.
mentor.show: Take one from the heap there, and put it here.
mentor.demo: Watch. I do another one here.
mentor.smaller: I put one part first. You do the rest.
mentor.share: We do it together. Half of it is yours.
mentor.raise: Fast, and right each time. Next time there is a bigger job for you.
mentor.break: Stop for a moment. Eat a rice ball first.
mentor.offer: Wave to me when you want help.
mentor.again.mark: Last time, a good look at the wrong part was enough for you.
mentor.again.cue: Last time, Nghé showed the place, and you did it.
mentor.again.demo: Last time, you watched one, and then you did it at once.
mentor.again.smaller: Last time, one part first helped you.
mentor.again.share: Last time we did it together, and you did it at once.
mentor.again.show: Last time, I showed how to take one, and you did it.
mentor.picture.bridge: You can walk around the village, and come back.
mentor.picture.cart: You can go and lay planks at the bridge, and come back.
mentor.picture.flood: You can go to the market and watch the coins, and come back.
mentor.picture.market: You can go to the fields and watch the water, and come back.
mentor.picture.duck: You can walk around, and come back to look again.
mentor.picture.scholar: You can help the healer at the herb beds, and come back.
mentor.picture.smith: You can go and watch the fisher at the river, and come back.
mentor.picture.fisher: You can go and watch the smith at the forge, and come back.
mentor.picture.healer: You can go and watch the teacher with the rods, and come back.
mentor.picture.woodcutter: You can go and watch the fisher at the river, and come back.
